As on 1st April, 2025, the following scheme of Tourna Limited was finalized for which necessary resolution was passed and approvals were obtained from appropriate authorities. Accordingly, it was decided that:

  1. Each equity share is to be sub-divided into ten fully paid-up equity shares of ₹10 each. After sub-division, each shareholder shall surrender to the company 40% of his holding, for the purpose of reissue to trade payables as necessary.
  2. Preference shareholders would give up 30% of their capital and 12% Debentures (face value ₹100 each) shall be issued to them for balance holdings.
  3. The company would issue additional 12% Debentures (face value ₹100 each) for ₹4,00,000 for meeting its working capital requirement and final settlement of Bank Overdraft at 90% of the amount.
  4. Existing debenture holders would accept Furniture & Fixture in full settlement of their dues.
  5. Trade payables claim shall be reduced to 70%, it is to be settled by the issue of equity shares of ₹10 each out of shares surrendered.
  6. The shares surrendered and not re-issued shall be cancelled.
  7. The taxation liability is to be settled at 50,000.
  8. Investment value to be reduced to market price.
  9. Balance of profit and loss account is to be written off.
  10. The value of inventories is to be increased by ₹32,000 and provision for Doubtful Debts is to be created at 5% of Trade Receivables.

You are required to: (i) Pass necessary journal entries in the books of account of Tourna Limited. (ii) Prepare Reconstruction Account, and (iii) Prepare Balance Sheet of the company after internal reconstruction. (14 Marks)

questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: A significant number of examinees failed to correctly compute the surrendered shares available for re-issue to trade payables after equity sub-division, and several also omitted to route the settlement of debenture holders through the Reconstruction Account when furniture and fixtures were given in full settlement of their dues, instead treating it as a direct asset disposal without recognising the resulting gain.

questions.why: Rank 29 topic (Methods of internal reconstruction); MTP January 2026 Set 1.
questions.question_html: Summarized Balance Sheet of Vijay Ltd. as on 31st March, 2025: Equity Shares of ₹10 each 3,50,000; 8% Cumulative Preference Shares of ₹100 each 1,75,000; 6% Debentures of ₹100 each 1,40,000; Sundry Creditors 1,75,000; Provision for taxation 3,500; Total 8,43,500. Assets: PPE 4,37,500; Investments (Market value ₹33,250) 35,000; Current Assets 3,50,000; P&L A/c (Dr.) 21,000; Total 8,43,500. Scheme of Internal Reconstruction approved and effective 31st March, 2025: (1) Investments brought to market value; (2) Taxation liability settled at ₹5,250 out of Current Assets; (3) balance of P&L written off; (4) equity shares reduced to ₹4 each; (5) preference shares reduced to ₹60 each; (6) debenture rate increased to 9%, debenture holders surrender ₹100 debentures and exchange 1-for-1 for fresh ₹80 debentures; (7) balance Current Assets revalued at ₹1,57,500; (8) PPE written down to 80%; (9) one creditor of ₹70,000 gives up 50% of claim, allotted 8,750 equity shares of ₹4 each in settlement. Pass Journal entries.
questions.answer_html:
Journal entries (books of Vijay Ltd.):

  1. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 1,750; To Investments A/c 1,750 (investments revalued to market value).
  2. (a) Provision for taxation A/c Dr. 3,500; Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 1,750; To Liability for taxation 5,250 (tax liability ascertained). (b) Liability for Taxation Dr. 5,250; To Current Assets (Bank) 5,250 (tax paid).
  3. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 21,000; To Profit & Loss A/c 21,000 (P&L debit balance written off).
  4. Equity Share Capital (₹10) A/c Dr. 3,50,000; To Equity Share Capital (₹4) A/c 1,40,000; To Capital Reduction A/c 2,10,000 (conversion of equity capital).
  5. 8% Cumulative Preference Share Capital A/c Dr. 1,75,000; To 8% Cumulative Preference Share Capital A/c 1,05,000; To Capital Reduction A/c 70,000 (conversion of preference capital to ₹60 each).
  6. 6% Debentures A/c Dr. 1,40,000; To 9% Debentures A/c 1,12,000; To Capital Reduction A/c 28,000 (fresh ₹80 debentures issued to existing holders).
  7. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 1,87,250; To Current Assets A/c 1,87,250 (current assets revalued).
  8. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 87,500; To Property, Plant & Equipment A/c 87,500 (PPE written down to 80%).
  9. Sundry Creditors A/c Dr. 70,000; To Equity Share Capital (₹4) A/c 35,000; To Capital Reduction A/c 35,000 (creditor's claim settled 50% cash-equivalent-in-shares, 50% given up).
  10. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 43,750; To Capital Reserve A/c (balancing figure) 43,750 (balance of Capital Reduction transferred to Capital Reserve).
questions.mistake_text: Author’s Note: Some examinees missed crediting Capital Reduction for the "gain" side of each conversion entry (e.g. the difference between old and new share/debenture face values), recording only the reduction without recognising the corresponding Capital Reduction credit.

Assets: Building at cost less depreciation 5,00,000; Plant at cost less depreciation 3,35,000; Trademarks and goodwill at cost 3,97,500; Inventory 5,00,000; Trade Receivables 4,10,000; Total 21,42,500. (Preference dividend in arrears 5 years.) Scheme of reconstruction: (i) equity shares reduced ₹50→₹5, shareholders subscribe 3 new equity shares of ₹5 for each held; (ii) preference shareholders forego dividend arrears, accept 4 new 6% preference shares of ₹10 plus 3 new equity shares of ₹5 for each ₹50 preference share; (iii) lenders convert ₹1,87,500 of loan into 15,000 new preference shares of ₹10 plus 7,500 new equity shares of ₹5; (iv) directors subscribe cash for 25,000 new equity shares of ₹5 (in addition to (i)); (v) ₹2,50,000 of cash received used to reduce the loan; (vi) equity capital cancelled applied to write off the P&L debit balance and ₹43,750 from plant, balance to write down trademarks/goodwill; nominal capital increased to ₹8,12,500 (preference) and ₹9,37,500 (equity). Pass journal entries and prepare the post-reconstruction Balance Sheet.

  1. Equity Share Capital A/c (₹50) Dr. 9,37,500; To Equity Share Capital A/c (₹5) 93,750; To Capital Reduction A/c 8,43,750 (equity capital reduced to ₹5 nominal).

  6. Equity Share Application A/c Dr. 1,25,000; To Equity Share Capital A/c 1,25,000 (application money transferred).
  7. Loan A/c Dr. 2,50,000; To Bank A/c 2,50,000 (loan repaid from cash proceeds).
  8. Capital Reduction A/c Dr. 7,68,750; To Profit and Loss A/c 5,63,750; To Plant A/c 43,750; To Trademarks and Goodwill A/c (balancing figure) 1,61,250 (losses/assets written off).

questions.question_html:
Sky Limited has decided to reconstruct the Balance Sheet since it has accumulated huge losses. The following is the balance sheet of the company as on 31st March, 2025 before reconstruction (₹ in lakh): Share Capital 4,200; Reserves and Surplus (1,566); Long term Borrowings 2,100; Trade Payables 306; Other Liabilities 72; Total 5,112. Assets: PPE 2,250; Current Investments 600; Inventories 900; Trade Receivables 1,350; Cash and Cash Equivalents 12; Total 5,112.

Notes to Accounts: Share Capital — Authorised: 600 lakh shares of ₹10 each 6,000; 24 lakh, 8% Preference Shares of ₹100 each 2,400; Total 8,400. Issued, Subscribed and Paid up: 300 lakh Equity Shares of ₹10 each, fully paid up 3,000; 12 lakh 8% Preference Shares of ₹100 each, fully paid up 1,200; Total 4,200. Reserves and Surplus: Debit balance of Profit and Loss A/c (1,566). Long Term Borrowings: 6% Debentures (Secured by Freehold Property) 1,200; Director's Loan 900; Total 2,100. Trade Payables: Trade payables for Goods 306. Other Liabilities: Interest Accrued and Due on 6% Debentures 72. PPE: Freehold Property 1,650; Plant & Machinery 600; Total 2,250. Current Investment: Investment in Equity Instruments 600. Inventories: Finished Goods 900. Trade Receivables: Trade receivables for Goods 1,350. Cash and Cash Equivalents: Balance with Bank 12.

The Board of Directors of the company decided upon the following scheme of reconstruction: (1) Preference Shares are to be written down to ₹75 each and Equity Shares to ₹2 each. (2) Preference Shares Dividend in arrears for 3 years to be waived by 2/3rd and for balance 1/3rd, Equity Shares of ₹2 each to be allotted. (3) Debenture holders agreed to take one Freehold Property at its book value of ₹900 lakh in part payment of their holding. Balance Debentures to remain as liability of the company. (4) Interest accrued and due on Debentures to be paid in cash. (5) Remaining Freehold Property to be valued at ₹1,100 lakh. (6) All investments sold out for ₹850 lakh. (7) 70% of Directors' loan to be waived and for the balance, Equity Shares of ₹2 each issue. (8) 40% of Trade receivables and 80% of Inventories to be written off. (9) Company's contractual commitments amounting to ₹1,800 lakh have been settled by paying 8% penalty of contract value.

You are required to: (a) Pass Journal Entries for all the transactions related to internal reconstruction; (b) Prepare Capital Reduction Account, Bank Account; and (c) Prepare Notes to Accounts on Share Capital & PPE, immediately after the implementation of internal reconstruction.

Given below is the Balance Sheet of ABC Ltd. as at March 31, 2026: Share Capital ₹18,50,000; Reserve and Surplus (₹6,53,000); Long-term borrowings ₹6,78,000; Trade Payables ₹3,57,000; Other Current Liabilities ₹85,000; Total ₹23,17,000. Assets: PPE ₹9,78,000; Intangible assets ₹4,50,000; Inventories ₹5,39,000; Trade Receivables ₹3,50,000; Total ₹23,17,000.

Notes to Accounts: Share Capital – 21,000 Equity Shares of ₹50 each ₹10,50,000; 16,000, 8% Cumulative Preference Shares of ₹50 each ₹8,00,000 (preference dividend in arrears for 3 years); Total ₹18,50,000. Reserve and Surplus – Debit balance of P&L Account (₹6,53,000). Long-term borrowings – 6% Debentures ₹6,78,000. Other current liabilities – Interest payable on debentures ₹40,680; Outstanding wages & salaries ₹44,320; Total ₹85,000. PPE – Building at cost less depreciation ₹5,00,000; Plant and machinery at cost less depreciation ₹4,78,000; Total ₹9,78,000. Intangible Assets – Goodwill ₹1,25,000; Trademarks ₹3,25,000; Total ₹4,50,000.

Since the company was not earning profits, it was decided to reconstruct the company. A summary of the reconstruction scheme: (i) The equity shareholders agreed their ₹50 shares should be reduced to ₹10 by cancellation of ₹40 per share, and to subscribe for three new equity shares of ₹10 each for each equity share held. (ii) The preference shareholders agreed to waive off the arrear of dividends, and to accept for each ₹50 share, 4 new 5% preference shares of ₹10 each fully paid up, plus one new equity share of ₹10 each fully paid up. (iii) The debenture holders accepted the inventories at an agreed figure of ₹5,20,000 and ₹1,48,680 in cash and forego the remaining amount due to them. (iv) Building is to be revalued at ₹6,50,000. (v) A contingent liability for which no provision had been made was settled at ₹10,800, of which ₹4,800 was recovered from insurance. (vi) The debit balance of Profit and Loss account is to be written off. (vii) Any balance remaining is first used to write down the value of goodwill and then applied to trademarks.

You are required to pass necessary journal entries to record the above reconstruction in the books of ABC Limited. (8 Marks)

The business of MA Limited was being carried on continuously at losses.
